title: The magi and the flight (Matthew 2:1–23)
hookLine: strangers from the east follow a star, then the family runs to Egypt as refugees
tomorrow: how do you lose a twelve-year-old for three whole days?

lines: NINE HOURS FOR A STRANGER'S BABY?
WHERE IS HE THAT IS BORN KING?
cards: Your maps app says nine hours. Would you drive that to see a baby you'd never met, in a country that isn't yours?

Matthew says strangers did more: magi from the east, following a star into Jerusalem and asking, in the Douay-Rheims Bible, "Where is he that is born king of the Jews? For we have seen his star in the east, and are come to adore him."
King Herod hears it, and Matthew says he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.

teach.b: The star brings them to the house in Bethlehem. They kneel and open their treasures: gold, frankincense and myrrh. Now what Matthew doesn't say.
He never says three; tradition counted three, likely from the gifts. He never calls them kings, and Caspar, Melchior and Balthasar are names from later tradition.
They're foreigners, the first in Matthew's Gospel to worship Jesus.
So the feast is the Epiphany, from the Greek for a showing: Christ shown to the whole world.

teach.h: C + M + B OVER THE DOOR.
teach.b: One to tell a friend: an old Epiphany custom chalks the new year over the front door around the letters C, M and B, the magi's traditional initials and a Latin blessing, may Christ bless this house. Then the story turns.
Joseph, the man who never speaks, dreams again: "Arise, and take the child and his mother, and fly into Egypt." They leave by night, across a border.
Herod orders the killing of Bethlehem's baby boys, whom the Church remembers as the Holy Innocents.
Pope Pius the Twelfth called the exiled Holy Family the model of every family forced to flee.

how: Catholics celebrate the Epiphany on January 6 or the nearest Sunday; in many places the door is blessed with chalk, and the Church remembers the Holy Innocents on December 28.

o: a showing: Christ revealed to the whole world
a sudden idea that strikes like lightning
a solemn vow spoken aloud before God and witnesses

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.

s: Matthew says there were three kings
he says magi, from the east. three comes from the three gifts; kings came later.
Epiphany means a showing or an appearing
Christ shown to the whole world, through strangers from the east.
Matthew names the magi Caspar, Melchior and Balthasar
he never names them. the names come from later tradition.

games.q: in January your neighbor chalks "C+M+B" and the year over her front door. you ask why. what is she most likely marking?
o: the Epiphany: the magi's visit, and a blessing on the house.
the three kings' birthdays, from the Gospel of Matthew.
a leftover Christmas decoration from her parish.
games.why: it's an Epiphany custom: the magi's traditional initials, and the Latin for may Christ bless this house.

practice: Stand up and hold out your hands as if each could carry one thing on a night you had to leave home: which two things would you take?

Keep that posture while you think of one family somewhere who left like that, as Mary and Joseph did. If you pray, you can pray for them in the name of the Holy Family; if not, just hold them in mind and hope for them.

wordCard.voice: Epiphany. A showing: Christ revealed to strangers from the east, before his own family runs for their lives.

orig.note: Greek: an appearing, a showing forth. the name of the feast of the magi.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: the holy family were refugees, strangers in Egypt until Herod was gone. Four weeks, done.
